scope: Reusable rules; private evidence is recorded separately.

rules.title: Give the reader a question worth answering
preservation_checks: Reader difficulty and purpose of the method remain explicit.

rules.title: Give each paragraph one job and each transition a reason
preservation_checks: Each paragraph has a job.
Sentence relations carry reasons; connectors alone cannot repair gaps.

rules.title: State the author's research choice
preservation_checks: Preserve the author's reason for the research choice.

rules.title: Recall the background that the current argument needs
preservation_checks: Recall the background needed now and verify its cross-reference.

rules.title: Lead with the supported result
preservation_checks: State supported findings with comparator and scope.
Keep predictive performance separate from device agreement.

rules.title: Make the ending answer the opening
preservation_checks: The ending answers the current opening.
Preserve useful navigation at its proper level.

rules.title: Give the construction before its parts
preservation_checks: Purpose and whole construction precede components.

rules.title: Define each object before using it
preservation_checks: Name, symbol, space and role precede use.
Check captions, abstract and moved definitions.

rules.title: Give equations an explanatory role
preservation_checks: Explain equation purpose and consequence.
Use consistent resource units and precision targets.

rules.title: Build diagrams in the reader's learning order
preservation_checks: Diagrams follow concept dependencies and preserve source credit.

rules.title: Give related terms explicit conditions of use
preservation_checks: Equivalences retain conventions, connectivity, ordering and subspace conditions.

rules.title: Label the kind of claim
preservation_checks: Separate theorem, prior result, observation, interpretation and proposal.

rules.title: Carry assumptions into the actual claim
preservation_checks: The printed claim retains assumptions, quantifiers and tested scope.

rules.title: Verify the source and its use
preservation_checks: Verify primary source identity and exact support for its use.

rules.title: Verify the object that the experiment computes
preservation_checks: Trace the implemented object, data version, metric and aggregation.

rules.title: Check proofs with independent evidence
preservation_checks: Keep independent proof checks, failed cases and tolerances.
Finite checks remain finite evidence.

rules.title: Give citations the work they can perform
preservation_checks: Citations support the associated claim and preserve useful attribution.

rules.title: Cut empty requirements and significance claims
preservation_checks: Replace significance claims with a concrete requirement or implication.

rules.title: Name useful future work
preservation_checks: Name the future study and the question it would answer.

rules.title: Put detail where the reader needs it
preservation_checks: Keep a destination for each necessary contribution and condition.

rules.title: Remove repeated jobs, not every repeated word
preservation_checks: Cut repeated jobs while retaining necessary definitions and navigation.

rules.title: Preserve distinctions that change meaning
preservation_checks: Preserve distinctions among objects, estimators, metrics and evidence types.

rules.title: Use a clear actor and a precise verb
preservation_checks: Use an actor and verb that name the actual scientific relation.

rules.title: Avoid formulaic turns of phrase
preservation_checks: Remove rhetorical correction, filler, fragments and mechanical emphasis.

rules.title: Use style metrics as prompts for reading
preservation_checks: Metrics prompt contextual reading; scores cannot establish quality or acceptance.

rules.title: Place each figure with the claim it supports
preservation_checks: Keep the figure near its supporting claim and inspect the rendered pages.

rules.title: Make captions self-contained at the right level
preservation_checks: Captions retain metric, units, uncertainty and relevant conditions.

rules.title: Present formal results consistently
preservation_checks: Formal statements retain assumptions, proof pointers and consistent presentation.

rules.title: Record the scope of each approval
preservation_checks: Acceptance records the exact unit, version, response and accepted scope.

rules.title: Preserve a recoverable baseline
preservation_checks: Preserve and restore the chosen baseline when the direction is rejected.

rules.title: Keep readiness states separate
preservation_checks: Evidence, editorial readiness, layout and author acceptance remain separate.

rules.title: Use critics as evidence-producing reviewers
preservation_checks: Critics report passages, evidence and reasons, including reasons to keep text.
